facts.text: Precision Reaction Wheel Assembly was deployed at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit during Kepler Space Telescope in 2009.
facts.source: NASA Ames K2 Mission Planning Guide / Howell et al.

facts.text: Set of four flywheels spun at thousands of RPM to impart gyroscopic torque for steady sub-arcsecond pointing without expending thruster propellant.
facts.source: NASA Ames K2 Mission Planning Guide / Howell et al.

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.

When two reaction wheels failed, engineers invented the 'K2 Mission', using solar radiation pressure balanced against the spacecraft body as a virtual third reaction wheel — extending the mission by four years!
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit.
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration on the Moon.

scenes.kids: I am Precision Reaction Wheel Assembly. I arrived here at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit in 2009.
scenes.explorer: Precision Reaction Wheel Assembly, Kepler Space Telescope: deployed at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit in 2009.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.
scenes.explorer: Set of four flywheels spun at thousands of RPM to impart gyroscopic torque for steady sub-arcsecond pointing without expending thruster propellant.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
scenes.explorer: Designed to withstand radiation, cosmic dust, and extreme temperature swings without failing.

scenes.kids: When two reaction wheels failed, engineers invented the 'K2 Mission', using solar radiation pressure balanced against the spacecraft body as a virtual third reaction wheel — extending the mission by four years!
scenes.explorer: When two reaction wheels failed, engineers invented the 'K2 Mission', using solar radiation pressure balanced against the spacecraft body as a virtual third reaction wheel — extending the mission by four years!

scenes.kids: My mission finished, but I stay here resting peacefully on the surface.
scenes.explorer: Fate: left on surface. Position recorded at coordinates [-1.8, 1.6].

scenes.kids: Everything I learned showed humanity how to explore deeper into space.
scenes.explorer: A milestone in planetary science and permanent historical artifact.
